summary: The exact real-axis target and its eta-based paper derivation were audited, but proof-assistant acceptance is blocked at the executable layer because Lean and Lake are not callable in the current environment.

value_assessment.novelty: Relative to the supplied unreviewed orbit-pruning artifacts, this independently reproduces the missing-toolchain obstruction in the current attempt, isolates it as preceding every Mathlib declaration question, sharpens eta positivity to a quantitative bound, and removes prefactor negativity from the minimal nonvanishing dependency set. It does not reproduce machine acceptance.
value_assessment.evidence: A deterministic application-resolution checker completed with exit code 2 after reporting both Lean and Lake absent, and an independent PATH locator found no matches; a separate inventory also found Elan absent. A written derivation states the exact theorem, proves a quantitative eta lower bound on paper, and audits the minimal eta-nonvanishing plus continuation-identity interface. The final structured-artifact check passed with two claims and one proposed task.
value_assessment.falsifier: A clean environment in which Lean and Lake resolve and the exact theorem compiles with audited imports would overturn the environment-level obstruction; a counterexample to any step in the written eta sign derivation would overturn the paper-level claim.

claims.statement: In the current process environment, the requested clean Lean acceptance cannot be performed because neither the Lean nor Lake application is callable.
claims.evidence_summary: Application-only discovery reported both tools absent and the deterministic checker terminated with its documented missing-tool status and exit code 2; an independent PATH locator found no matches.
claims.verification_method: Run the deterministic environment checker in the same process environment and confirm the missing-tool status and nonzero exit.

claims.statement: At paper-proof level, for every real x strictly between zero and one, eta positivity plus the eta-zeta continuation identity implies zeta(x) is nonzero; proving the prefactor negative is needed only for the stronger conclusion that zeta(x) is negative.
claims.evidence_summary: Consecutive pairing gives eta(x) at least 1 minus 2 to the negative x, which is positive. Substituting a hypothetical zero zeta value into eta(x) equals A(x) times zeta(x) forces eta(x) to be zero, a contradiction.
claims.verification_method: Formalize alternating-series convergence, the paired-partial-sum eta bound, the continuation identity, and compatible coercions, then compile the quantified nonvanishing theorem in a clean proof-assistant environment.

limitations: No theorem was accepted by a proof assistant in this attempt.
The missing executable layer prevents determining whether the smallest subsequent issue is an absent library theorem, eta identity, convergence lemma, positivity lemma, or coercion lemma.
The analytic continuation identity is an explicit input to the paper proof and was not formalized here.
No conclusion is made about nonreal zeros or the Riemann Hypothesis.
failed_approaches: Clean compilation could not begin because the required Lean and Lake applications are absent.
Library declaration discovery could not be performed because there is no callable toolchain or local Mathlib source in the attempt directory.
next_actions: Repeat the check in a clean Lean and Mathlib environment, query first for a direct zeta nonvanishing or sign theorem, and otherwise formalize the minimal eta-nonvanishing plus continuation-identity argument.
Compile the exact real-axis theorem with explicit imports and record every non-core declaration used.

proposed_tasks.title: Compile the real-axis zeta sign lemma
proposed_tasks.objective: In a clean Lean and Mathlib environment, prove that zeta at a real x is nonzero whenever zero is less than x and x is less than one.
proposed_tasks.rationale: This removes the explicit real-axis exclusion assumption from the orbit-pruning formalization and resolves whether Mathlib supplies the needed direct theorem or the minimal eta-nonvanishing and continuation-identity ingredients.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: The exact quantified theorem compiles with explicit imports and an audit of all non-core declarations.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Identify the first missing or mismatched declaration after the toolchain starts, including its expected type and the compiler diagnostic.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Build from a clean project, rerun after clearing build products, and inspect the theorem dependencies and imports.
